eips.title: Align Checkpoint with Epoch Boundary Block
eips.summary: Withdrawn by Lodestar team as they decided decouple consensus makes it unnecessary.

moments.context: Stokes announced EIP-8333 (Align Checkpoint with Epoch Boundary Block) has been withdrawn. Cayman from Lodestar explained they looked further into decoupled consensus and decided it was not worth dealing with now.

eips.title: Anti-Correlation Attestation Penalties
eips.summary: Oisin Kyne posted a chat update noting the 2026 revision has been merged and asking teams to consider it for CFI.

moments.context: Oisin shared in chat that the 2026 update to EIP-7716 (Anti-Correlation Attestation Penalties) has been merged, linked a calculator/FAQ site, and asked people to consider squeezing it into CFI as a B-tier in Hegota.

eips.title: Tapered Issuance Burn
eips.summary: Withdrawn by its champions who will pursue a broader community-driven process outside ACD scoping.

moments.context: Stokes announced EIP-8363 (Tapered Issuance Burn) has been withdrawn. The champions decided that shoehorning this policy change into ACD scoping was not the right approach and posted a new timeline on ETH Magicians for a community-driven process.

eips.title: Disallow new 0x00 validators
eips.summary: Updated to keep only the deposit guard; forced exit split into a separate future EIP. CFI'd on this call.

moments.context: NC explained the EIP was updated per last call's request: the deposit guard for disallowing new 0x00 validators remains, while the forced exit part becomes a standalone EIP not proposed for Hegota. The call agreed to CFI it with broad support in the chat.

eips.title: Remove `deposit` and `eth1data` fields
eips.summary: Referenced as an example of a simple EIP when discussing implementation difficulty of other proposals.

moments.context: Stokes noted that 8015 had already been CFI'd previously.
Terence referenced 8015 as an example of an easy EIP, contrasting it with the engineering challenge of quick slots.

eips.title: Fast Execution Payload Broadcast
eips.summary: Held for later in scoping as it was proposed late; Lodestar team expressed DFI preference in chat.

moments.context: Stokes proposed holding EIP-8411 (Fast Execution Payload Broadcast) until later in scoping since it was proposed late and some clients had not yet weighed in.
In chat, Cayman said Lodestar's opinion is DFI, wanting more mainnet data first and wanting to keep fork scope smaller.

eips.title: Custom sweep threshold for validators
eips.summary: Mentioned in chat as a prerequisite for potentially disallowing new 0x01 validators in a future fork.

moments.context: Chat discussion about whether to disallow new 0x01 validators referenced EIP-8148 (custom sweep threshold) as needing to land first, with potuz saying if 8148 gets in then 0x01 should be disabled at the same fork.

eips.title: Quick Slots
eips.summary: Quick Slots proposal to reduce slot time from 12s to 10s was CFI'd after extensive debate about PQ concerns and testing.

moments.context: Barnabé Monnot presented slides making the case for CFI of quick slots in Hegota, citing ecosystem support, merged specs, Prysm prototype, and smart contract outreach.
Matthew Keil from Lodestar argued against inclusion, citing PQ concerns and that decoupled consensus would rework slot mechanics, suggesting adding the machinery but not reducing slot time yet.
Terence confirmed Prysm rated it A, has a prototype, and believes the tradeoff is worth it. Enrico from Teku rated it S and considers implementation not complicated.
Stokes distilled rough consensus: everyone agrees on the value, CFI today with the understanding that more data is needed before SFI, and it can be pulled out if issues arise. The call agreed to CFI.

eips.title: Move committee index outside Attestation
eips.summary: Dustin compared quick slots to the 7549 experience in terms of testing drag risk.

moments.context: Dustin said quick slots has a 7549 feel for him in terms of the long tail of testing potentially dragging on the fork.

eips.title: Withdrawal credentials preregistration
eips.summary: Mentioned in chat alongside EIP-8148 as proposals someone wanted CFI'd with a timebox approach.

moments.context: Dima Gusakov asked in chat whether the timebox-and-kick-out approach proposed for quick slots could also apply to EIP-8148 and EIP-8205.

eips.title: Top-up Sync
eips.summary: Top-up Sync debated at length; DFI'd as an optional proposal that teams can pursue outside the fork.

moments.context: Dustin presented Top-up Sync as enabling CL-driven EL sync, reducing duplicate gossip, improving resilience, and enabling flexible storage deduplication via a new engine API endpoint.
Łukasz raised concerns about loss of EL control over sync optimization. Dustin clarified nothing is mandatory for ELs.
Enrico argued that without deciding the end-game CL/EL responsibility split, shipping this is premature. Stokes concluded with DFI, noting teams can still experiment with it outside the fork.

eips.title: Independent CL/EL Sync
eips.summary: Referenced as a previously DFI'd alternative approach to EL sync that delegated sync to the EL.

moments.context: Francesco Risitano mentioned EIP-8237 (Independent CL/EL Sync) as an alternative that was DFI'd, which took the approach of delegating EL sync fully to the EL with a binding commitment.

eips.title: Reduce CL Block Retention Window
eips.summary: Reduce CL Block Retention Window deferred to next call as clients had not reviewed it yet.

moments.context: Kevaundray Wedderburn said he was okay skipping it if clients had not looked into it. Barnabas suggested deferring to the next call. Stokes agreed and asked everyone to review it before then.

eips.title: Optional Execution Proofs
eips.summary: Optional Execution Proofs debated briefly; Łukasz raised security and governance concerns; deferred to next call.

moments.context: Ignacio proposed CFI for optional execution proofs. Łukasz objected on two grounds: shipping something not production-secure sends mixed signals, and having zkVM/guest-program pairs chosen by committee breaks the open culture of client development. Ignacio responded that these concerns apply more to mandatory proofs, not to this optional spec. Discussion was deferred to the next call.
